title: ‘Nightmare Scenario’: Zero-Click Spyware Is Infecting Phones via Targeted Ads
gist: Citizen Lab documented 'AdFection', the first detailed public evidence of mercenary spyware (Candiru) delivered zero-click through ads served by Israeli-founded Discover-Tech, hitting 45 Al Jazeera devices in 2024-25. Ad impressions linked to the firm reached 70,000+ apps and 120,000+ websites, exposing the ad-bidding stack as an unvetted attack surface; Google, IAB Europe and Beeswax have cut the firm off.

insights.claim: Citizen Lab reports the first detailed, publicly available technical evidence of sophisticated spyware infecting devices through digital ads, with no user interaction required.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Ad-delivered zero-click exploitation moves from theoretical to documented, raising the security risk premium on the ad-tech supply chain.

insights.claim: During 2024 and 2025 Citizen Lab concluded that 45 Al Jazeera devices were targeted with zero-click attacks delivered via ads issued by Discover-Tech and distributing spyware attributed to Israeli developer Candiru.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Media organisations and other high-value targets face state-grade ad-borne threats; watch for further attributions to commercial spyware vendors.

insights.claim: Discover-Tech's Controlium advertising platform can reportedly 'de-anonymize, fingerprint, and automatically infect devices' once an ad appears, and researchers estimate millions of devices were directed to Candiru's servers for profiling.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: The scale (millions profiled, a fraction infected) shows targeting is selective; the ad platform itself functions as the exploit delivery and triage layer.
insights.quote: de-anonymize, fingerprint, and automatically infect devices
insights.locator: The Citizen Lab researchers say that Discover-Tech operates

insights.claim: Exposed ad-bidding records show ads tied to Discover-Tech with attacker script tags ran in more than 70,000 mobile apps and more than 120,000 websites between March and June 2026, with multiple apps showing over a million such ads.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Reach this broad means publishers and exchanges carry latent exposure; expect tighter vendor vetting costs across programmatic ad supply.

insights.claim: Discover-Tech ad impressions were seen on government and national-security-linked networks including NATO and United Nations networks, European lawmaking bodies, Australian critical infrastructure providers, and armed forces and agencies in Norway and Sweden, although not all ads were weaponized.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Government and critical-infrastructure networks without strict ad blocking are exposed; this supports demand for network-level ad filtering and endpoint security.
insights.locator: The firm's ads weren't necessarily all weaponized

insights.claim: The ability to push individualized, arbitrary content to specific users, a hallmark of the modern ad ecosystem, is ideally suited to the mercenary spyware industry, and abuse will continue until the architecture changes or ad companies seriously vet customers.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Regulatory or platform-level KYC requirements for ad buyers are a plausible catalyst; ad-tech firms with weak vetting carry tail risk.
insights.quote: Until this architecture changes, or ad companies get serious about customer vetting, we’re going to keep seeing this kind of abuse.
insights.locator: “The ability to push individualized, arbitrary content

insights.claim: Individuals have little defence against zero-click ad attacks other than blocking ads as thoroughly as possible on all websites and platforms, a practice Citizen Lab says intelligence agencies such as the NSA and CIA appear well aware of.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Ad blocking shifts from privacy convenience to security control, a potential tailwind for ad-blocker and DNS-filtering vendors and a headwind for ad-funded publishers.
insights.locator: The situation is so concerning, he notes

insights.claim: Real-time bidding lets advertisers collect large volumes of device, location and browsing data within milliseconds, a long-standing privacy problem in which data brokers sell personal information that law enforcement and hostile nations buy to track people.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: The same data pipes that drive ad targeting also enable surveillance and exploit targeting, strengthening the case for privacy regulation of RTB.
insights.locator: Often when you see ads online or in apps

insights.claim: Prior zero-click ad-delivered spyware campaigns rarely surfaced publicly, likely because ad infrastructure is trusted everywhere without specific oversight and defenders lack visibility; Al Jazeera's network logs were key to detecting this one.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Absence of past reports reflects a visibility gap, not rarity, so assume more undiscovered campaigns, especially against personal devices off monitored networks.
insights.quote: Defenders have to be in the right place at the right time, looking at the right data.
insights.locator: “The network logs from Al Jazeera were key

insights.claim: Google blocked Discover-Tech from its ad platforms for systematically violating policies after a joint investigation with Citizen Lab and Confiant, and added Safe Browsing warnings for websites linked to the group.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Platform takedowns are reactive after external researchers find the abuse; watch whether Google tightens advertiser verification.
insights.locator: Google, which operates one of the world's largest advertising businesses

insights.claim: IAB Europe suspended Discover-Tech from its global vendor list after an audit and says confirmation of the spyware findings could justify permanent expulsion; Comcast-owned Beeswax also removed the company from its platform.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Expulsion from the GVL and DSP platforms cuts a bad actor's market access; monitor for wider audits of smaller ad-tech vendors.
insights.locator: The European branch of the Interactive Advertising Bureau

insights.claim: Integrity Partners is believed to own Candiru's assets following US government sanctions on Candiru in 2021, indicating the spyware vendor's capabilities persisted despite sanctions.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Sanctions on spyware vendors appear to leak through asset transfers, a theme for policy and compliance risk on the mercenary spyware sector.

insights.claim: Digital Content Next CEO Jason Kint says he would not be entirely surprised by zero-click attacks through ads and that anything lowering trust in the open web is deeply concerning.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Publisher trade groups acknowledge the risk, which may become a lever for stricter supply-chain demands on ad partners.
insights.quote: Although rare and sophisticated, I wouldn’t be entirely surprised to learn about zero-click attacks through ads
insights.locator: Jason Kint, CEO of the digital media trade organization
